title: Physical quantities, modern SI & unit conversions
subtitle: Base vs derived quantities, the seven 2019 SI defining constants, dimensionless angles, and CGS conversion powers.
takeaway: Numerical value and unit size vary inversely (n1 u1 = n2 u2); SI mass base is the kilogram (10^3 g), NEVER the gram!

cards.title: Measurement invariant n1 u1 = n2 u2
items: Every physical quantity Q equals a pure number n times a reference unit u: Q = n1 u1 = n2 u2. Smaller units demand proportionally larger numerical values:
Common JEE trap (Q22): kilogram (kg), NOT gram (g), is the SI base unit of mass — 1 g is 10^-3 kg!

cards.title: All seven SI base quantities & modern definitions
items: Since 2019, all seven SI base units are fixed by locking exact numerical values of universal constants (zero artifact drift!):
Memorise exact symbols: length [L] (m), mass [M] (kg), time [T] (s), electric current [A] or [I] (A), temperature [Theta] or [K] (K), amount [N] (mol), luminous intensity [J] (cd).
Notice: charge C = A s is DERIVED in SI even though elementary charge e fixes the ampere via e = 1.602176634e-19 A s!

cards.title: Supplementary angles: named unit, NO dimensions!
items: Plane angle d(theta) = ds / r (unit: radian, rad) and solid angle d(Omega) = dA_perp / r^2 (unit: steradian, sr; full sphere = 4 pi sr) are ratios of lengths/areas:
Exam multi-correct classic: "Does a dimensionless quantity ALWAYS lack a unit?" NO — plane angle (rad) and solid angle (sr) have SI units yet zero dimensions!
Conversely, any quantity WITH non-zero dimensions MUST possess a unit — "unitless" ALWAYS implies "dimensionless", never the reverse!

cards.title: Six instant CGS / practical unit bridges
items: Keep standard CGS and atomic/practical conversions fluent so multi-unit numericals take 5 seconds instead of full exponent algebra:
Watch viscosity trap: 1 poise = 1 g/(cm s) = 0.1 Pa s (NOT 10 Pa s!). In water at 20 C, eta ~ 1 centipoise = 10^-3 Pa s!

title: Dimensional formulae I: mechanics, fluids & heat
subtitle: Reconstructing every formula from its simplest defining law, twin-dimension pairs, and thermal constants.
takeaway: Never memorise long exponents blindly: pick the shortest defining formula (F = G m^2/r^2, F = eta A dv/dy, P = sigma A T^4) and solve in 10 seconds!
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md sec. 3.3, C1, E1, Q14, Q25, P1, P10, P17, P21

cards.title: Core mechanics, elasticity & fluid dimensions
items: Anchor everything on [v] = [L T^-1], [a] = [L T^-2], [F] = [M L T^-2], and [E] = [W] = [M L^2 T^-2]:
Notice surface tension [M T^-2] matches spring constant k = F/x AND surface energy per unit area J/m^2 = [M L^2 T^-2]/[L^2]!

cards.title: Rotational & quantum action quantities
items: Angular coordinate theta is dimensionless, so every rotational variable differs from linear mechanics purely by powers of lever arm [L]:
Check Planck constant immediately from E = h f (P1): [h] = [M L^2 T^-2] / [T^-1] = [M L^2 T^-1] — identical to angular momentum L = m v r (Bohr quantisation L = n hbar)!
Work and torque share [M L^2 T^-2] (P17), yet torque is NEVER measured in joules (write N m) because work = r . F while torque = r x F!

cards.title: Thermal & radiation physical constants
items: Extract temperature [K] powers directly from P V = n R T, E = k_B T, Fourier conduction dQ/dt = -k_th A dT/dx, and Stefan-Boltzmann P = sigma A T^4:
Specific heat capacity c = Q/(m dT) drops mass cleanly: [c] = [L^2 T^-2 K^-1] (mass does NOT appear in specific heat or latent heat [L^2 T^-2]!).

cards.title: Truly dimensionless physical ratios to recognise
items: Examiners love hiding pure numbers inside multi-correct lists — spot these instantly as [M^0 L^0 T^0]:
Watch specific vs relative traps: relative density (specific gravity) rho/rho_water IS dimensionless [1], whereas density is [M L^-3] and specific heat is [L^2 T^-2 K^-1]!
Also watch "velocity gradient" dv/dx = [T^-1] vs "potential gradient" dV/dx = [-E] NOT dimensionless!

title: Dimensional formulae II: electromagnetism & shortcuts
subtitle: Exact [M L T A] powers of electric/magnetic fields and the golden composite blocks that bypass 4-variable algebra in JEE.
takeaway: Never expand eps0 and mu0 in JEE MCQs when composite blocks appear: [RC] = [L/R] = [sqrt(LC)] = [T] and [1/sqrt(mu0 eps0)] = [L T^-1]!
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md sec. 3.3 + JEE Advanced E&M dimensional bridges

cards.title: Four-step ladder from charge q = I t to V, E, R, C
items: Start from [q] = [A T] and potential V = W / q = [M L^2 T^-2] / [A T] = [M L^2 T^-3 A^-1]; every electric quantity falls out in one division:
Notice how C = eps0 A / d gives [eps0] = [C]/[L] instantly — 5x faster and safer than squaring r inside Coulomb law!

cards.title: Three-step ladder for B, magnetic flux Phi_B, L & mu0
items: Start from wire force F = I l B (NOT Biot-Savart!) to get [B], then Phi_B = B A and U = (1/2) L I^2:
Again solenoid inductance L = mu0 N^2 A / l gives [mu0] = [L_ind] / [L] in two seconds without touching 2 pi r!
Watch flux quantum Phi_0 = h / (2 e): since [h]/[q] = [M L^2 T^-1]/[A T] = [M L^2 T^-2 A^-1] = [Phi_B], it has exact Weber dimensions!

cards.title: Golden composite blocks (solve JEE questions in 5s!)
items: Nearly every JEE Main/Advanced E&M dimensional MCQ embeds known circuit/wave combinations disguised as products:
Example: "Dimensions of L I^2 / (C V)?" Spot L I^2 = energy, C V = q -> energy / q = potential [V]! Done in 4 seconds with ZERO M,L,T,A algebra!

cards.title: Atomic & quantum combinations popular in JEE Adv
items: Three recurring combinations across Modern Physics and E&M papers:
Fine-structure constant alpha ~ 1/137 has ZERO dimensions; Bohr magneton e hbar / (2 m_e) is a magnetic dipole moment m = I * Area = [A L^2]!
Electric dipole p = q d has [A T L], whereas magnetic dipole m = I A has [A L^2]: their ratio [p / m] is [T / L] = [1 / speed]!

title: Principle of homogeneity & transcendental functions
subtitle: Matching additive terms, transcendental pure-number gates, and dimensional traps with hidden constants or logs.
takeaway: You can ONLY add, subtract, or equate terms of identical dimensions, and arguments of exp, ln, sin, cos MUST be dimensionless [1].
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md sec. 3.4-3.5, C2, Q1, Q2

cards.title: Principle of homogeneity: term-by-term balance
items: In any physically valid equation A + B - C = D + E, every separated additive block MUST carry identical dimensions: [A] = [B] = [C] = [D] = [E].
Homogeneity is a fast filter: s = u t + a t fails immediately because [a t] = [L T^-1] != [L] (sec. 3.4); v = u + a t^2 fails because [a t^2] = [L] != [L T^-1] (C2).
Watch moles n! If Van der Waals is written for n moles (P + n^2 a / V^2)(V - n b) = n R T, then [a] includes mol^-2 and [b] is [L^3 mol^-1]!

cards.title: Transcendental pure-number gate: exp, ln, trig
items: Because exp(u) = 1 + u + u^2/2! + ... adds u to 1 and u^2 to u, both the input u AND output of exp, ln, sin, cos, tan MUST be dimensionless [1]:
Then [P] = [alpha / beta] gives [beta] = [alpha] / [P] = [M L T^-2] / [M L^-1 T^-2] = [L^2] in two lines (classic JEE Advanced question!).
Watch integrated log forms in chemistry/thermo: ln P = C - L/(R T) hides constant C = ln P0, meaning ln(P / P0) = -L/(R T)! Standalone ln(5 metros) is meaningless!

cards.title: Dimensions inside derivatives and integrals
items: Differentiation divides by the variable of differentiation, whereas integration multiplies by the differential dx:
JEE classic: find m in int dx / sqrt(2 a x - x^2) = a^m sin^-1(x/a - 1). Left side has [L] / sqrt([L^2]) = [L^0] = [1]! Since [sin^-1(...)] = [1], [a^m] = [1] => m = 0!
Many students guess m = 1 or -1 from memorised calculus tables forgetting 2 a x - x^2 has [a] = [x], so dx / sqrt(2ax - x^2) is ALREADY dimensionless!

cards.title: Necessary != sufficient: hidden constants & nth-second
items: Homogeneity is NECESSARY, never SUFFICIENT: s = u t + 5 a t^2 is dimensionally consistent yet physically wrong (missing 1/2).
FAMOUS JEE TRAP: displacement in the nth second s_n IS dimensionally valid because hidden factor (1 second) multiplies u and a (1 s)^2 on the right!
Hidden dimensional constants also lurk in empirical formulas like v = 331 + 0.6 T_C where "331" carries m/s and "0.6" carries m/(s K)!

title: Deriving relations, custom base units & limits
subtitle: Solving exponent systems cleanly, changing base units to [F, V, T] or [c, G, h], and the four hard limits of dimensional analysis.
takeaway: In 3 base dimensions [M, L, T], dimensional analysis solves AT MOST 3 unknown powers and NEVER determines dimensionless prefactors or functions!
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md sec. 3.5-3.6, C3, E2, E5, Q15, Q18, Q21

cards.title: Deriving scaling laws by matching exponents
items: Write target Y = k X1^a X2^b X3^c, expand both sides in [M, L, T], equate powers of M, L, T, and solve the 3 linear equations:
\mathrm{Drag\ (E2):}\ F = k \rho r^2 v^2;\qquad \mathrm{Blast\ (E5):}\ R = k\left(\frac{E t^2}{\rho}\right)^{1/5}
Sensitivity check (Q21): in Sedov-Taylor R ~ E^(1/5) t^(2/5) rho^(-1/5), doubling blast energy E only raises radius R by 2^(1/5) = 1.149 (+14.9%)!
Similarly for gas sound speed v(P, rho) (Q18): v = k sqrt(P / rho) (Newton k = 1 gives 289 m/s; Laplace k = sqrt(gamma) gives 343 m/s).

cards.title: Changing base units to [F, V, T] or [E, P, V] (JEE #1!)
items: When JEE asks for dimensions of mass or density in custom base system {Force F, Velocity V, Time T}, avoid big matrices by algebraic substitution:
Test whether three proposed base quantities {X, Y, Z} are VALID independent bases using the determinant of their exponent matrix in [M, L, T]:
CRITICAL CHECK: {Force F, Mass M, Acceleration a} CANNOT form a valid base system because F = M a makes det = 0 (cannot build [L] or [T] separately)!

cards.title: Planck scales from fundamental constants (c, G, h)
items: Combining relativistic c [L T^-1], gravitational G [M^-1 L^3 T^-2], and quantum h [M L^2 T^-1] uniquely defines Planck length, time, and mass:
Fast exam check: once you memorize or solve l_P = sqrt(G h / c^3), dividing by c gives t_P instantly without solving a second 3x3 system!
Same trick with {e^2/(4 pi eps0), c, G}: solving [L] gives classical/gravitational charge scale in 15 seconds.

cards.title: Four strict failure modes of dimensional analysis
items: State explicitly when dimensional derivation CANNOT complete a formula (sec. 3.5, C3, Q11):
1. Dimensionless constants: cannot find 2 pi in T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g) or 1/2 in (1/2) m v^2.
2. Dimensionless arguments: misses sin(theta) in torque r F sin(theta) and amplitude correction 1 + theta_0^2 / 16 in a large-angle pendulum.
3. More than 3 variables in mechanics (e.g. F depending on r, v, rho AND eta needs Reynolds function f(Re)!), OR sums of terms like s = u t + (1/2) a t^2.

title: Significant figures, scientific notation & rounding
subtitle: Exact counting rules, multiplication vs addition precision limits, IEEE round-to-even rule, and guard digits.
takeaway: Add/subtract keeps the FEWEST DECIMAL PLACES; multiply/divide keeps the FEWEST SIGNIFICANT FIGURES — never swap the two!
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md sec. 3.7, C4, C5, E6, Q3, Q16, Q20, P3

cards.title: Five ironclad rules for counting significant figures
items: 1. All non-zero digits and all trapped zeros between non-zeros count (1002 -> 4 sf). 2. Leading zeros NEVER count (0.00560 -> 3 sf, C4).
3. Trailing zeros AFTER a decimal point ALWAYS count (2.300 -> 4 sf; 0.00230e3 -> 3 sf, P3). 4. Unit change NEVER alters sig figs: 2.30 m = 230 cm = 0.00230 km = 2300 mm (write 2.30e3 mm!).
N = a \times 10^b \quad (1 \le |a| < 10):\ \ \text{sig figs of } N \equiv \text{digits in } a
Exact integers & definitions (2 in 2 pi r, 4/3 in sphere volume, speed of light c) have INFINITE significant figures and never limit an answer!

cards.title: Arithmetic precision rules: +/- vs x and /
items: Addition & subtraction follow DECIMAL PLACES (convert all terms to the SAME power of 10 first!):
Multiplication & division follow TOTAL SIGNIFICANT FIGURES (E6, C5, Q16):
Watch mixed powers in +/-: write 4.2e-3 + 3.15e-4 = (4.2 + 0.315)e-3 = 4.5e-3 (2 sig figs, NOT 3)!

cards.title: NCERT / JEE rounding rule when dropped digit is 5
items: Retain 1-2 extra guard digits through intermediate steps and round ONCE at the end:
Round-half-to-even eliminates upward bias across thousands of rounded numbers when the dropped tail is an exact 5000... (if ANY non-zero follows 5, ALWAYS round up!).
Watch subtle multi-step JEE questions like area of cube of side 7.203 m (4 sf): 6 * (7.203)^2 = 311.299 -> 311.3 m^2 (factor 6 is an exact face count!).

cards.title: Matching value digits to uncertainty digits (Q20)
items: An uncertainty dX must match the decimal place of the last reported digit of X: never leave orphan digits beyond the error bar!
Uncertainties themselves are reported to 1 significant figure (or 2 when leading digit is 1, e.g. +-0.15 in Q17: Z = 1.00 +- 0.15).
Order of magnitude convention: write N = a * 10^b with 1 <= a < 10; if a <= sqrt(10) ~ 3.16 (or <= 5 in school texts), order is 10^b, else 10^(b+1).

title: Error classification, accuracy vs precision & mean statistics
subtitle: Systematic vs random vs blunders, accuracy vs precision, JEE Main mean absolute error vs sample standard deviation.
takeaway: Averaging n trials cuts random standard error as 1/sqrt(n), NEVER removing systematic bias; distinguish spread sigma from mean uncertainty sigma/sqrt(n)!
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md sec. 3.8, 4.1, C6, C8, C12, E8, Q8, P6, P9, P24

cards.title: Systematic vs random vs gross blunders
items: 1. Systematic errors shift every reading reproducibly one way: zero offset (C6), miscalibrated scale, fixed parallax angle (P6), heat loss in calorimetry. Fix by calibration/model!
2. Random errors fluctuate unpredictably (+ and -) from air draughts, vibration, eye judgement. Reduced by repeating n independent measurements.
Trap 3 (sec. 8): a digital watch running 5 minutes fast reading 10:04:32.18 is high-PRECISION (0.01 s resolution) yet poor-ACCURACY (5 min bias)!

cards.title: NCERT / JEE Main mean-absolute-error protocol
items: In NCERT/JEE Main lab problems with n readings x_1, ..., x_n when standard deviation is NOT requested, compute arithmetic mean x_bar and mean absolute error:
Note carefully: residuals (x_i - x_bar) sum to ZERO algebraically, which is why absolute bars |x_i - x_bar| (or squares below) are mandatory!

cards.title: Sample standard deviation sigma vs SEM sigma/sqrt(n)
items: Rigorous JEE Advanced / Olympiad statistics uses Bessel (n - 1) sample standard deviation sigma for single-reading spread and sigma / sqrt(n) for the uncertainty of the MEAN (E8, P24):
Trap 9: do NOT report single-shot scatter sigma (0.016) when asked for the uncertainty of the best estimate x_bar (0.007), nor confuse n - 1 with n!

cards.title: Consistency check against a reference value (Q13)
items: Two independent measurements X +- dX and Y +- dY agree within experimental error when their difference sits inside combined uncertainty:
Quick check (Q13): measuring g = 9.81 +- 0.02 m/s^2 vs local reference 9.806 m/s^2 gives |9.81 - 9.806| = 0.004 <= 0.02 -> 100% consistent!
Never delete an awkward data point ("outlier") merely to shrink sigma unless your lab log confirms a specific physical blunder!

title: Error propagation: sums, powers & coupled formulas
subtitle: Absolute vs fractional rules, quadrature vs worst-case bounds, catastrophic cancellation, and the parallel-resistor trap.
takeaway: Sums add ABSOLUTE errors; products/powers add FRACTIONAL errors; if a variable appears TWICE (R1*R2/(R1+R2)), simplify FIRST before taking differentials!
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md sec. 3.9, E3, E7 (fixed!), Q4, Q5, Q17, P4, P8

cards.title: Sums & differences: ABSOLUTE errors add!
items: For Z = A + B or Z = A - B, worst-case error adds absolute errors directly; independent random errors combine in quadrature:
Catastrophic cancellation (P8): for A = 1.234 +- 0.001 and B = 1.231 +- 0.001, A - B = 0.003 +- 0.002 -> relative error jumps from 0.08% to 67%!

cards.title: Products, quotients & powers: log-differential rule
items: Take ln|Z| = p ln|A| + q ln|B| - r ln|C|, differentiate dZ/Z = p dA/A + q dB/B - r dC/C, then flip MINUS signs to PLUS for maximum uncertainty (P4):
Source E7 audit fix: sphere density rho = m / ((4/3) pi r^3) with m = 100 +- 1 g (1%), r = 2.00 +- 0.02 cm (1%) gives d(rho)/rho = 1% + 3(1%) = 4.0% (NOT 6% printed in E7 check box!).
For independent Gaussian random errors, quadrature replaces sum of terms by sqrt( (p dA/A)^2 + (q dB/B)^2 + (r dC/C)^2 ).

cards.title: CRITICAL JEE ADV TRAP: parallel resistors & thin lenses!
items: NEVER apply quotient + sum rules separately to R_eq = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) or f = u v / (u + v), because dR1 in numerator partially cancels dR1 in denominator! Differentiate 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 directly:
Test R1 = R2 = 100 +- 1 Ohm: R_eq = 50 Ohm, exact dR_eq = 2500 * (2 / 10000) = 0.50 Ohm (1.0%), whereas naive quotient rule gives 3.0% (3x wrong!).

cards.title: General single/multi-variable calculus rule
items: For ANY smooth function Z = f(x, y) (including logs, trig, exponentials — where power rules do not apply!), use first-order partial derivatives:
\Delta Z_{\max} = \left|\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\right|\Delta x + \left|\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}\right|\Delta y
Handy specials: if Z = ln(x), dZ = dx / x (ABSOLUTE error in ln x equals RELATIVE error in x!). If Z = sin(theta), dZ = |cos(theta)| d(theta_in_RADIANS!).
ALWAYS convert angle uncertainty d(theta) from degrees into RADIANS (multiply by pi / 180) before differentiating sin(theta) or tan(theta)!

title: Vernier callipers: standard, general (m/n) & retro-vernier
subtitle: Exact 1 MSD - 1 VSD derivation, zero-error sign discipline, non-standard JEE Advanced verniers, and K-step coincidence.
takeaway: Never memorise LC = 1 mm / n blindly: ALWAYS compute 1 MSD and 1 VSD from the question stem first using LC = 1 MSD - 1 VSD!
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md sec. 3.10, E4, Q6, P5, P15, P22 + JEE Adv verniers

cards.title: General least-count formula (works on ALL verniers!)
items: Suppose n divisions on the vernier scale span m divisions on the main scale (m < n in standard forward verniers), where 1 main-scale division is 1 MSD:
Standard case m = n - 1 gives LC = (1/n) MSD (e.g. 10 VSD = 9 mm -> 0.1 mm; 20 VSD = 19 mm -> 0.05 mm, P5).
JEE ADV FAVORITE: if 10 VSD = 8 MSD with 1 MSD = 1 mm, LC = (1 - 8/10) mm = 0.2 mm (NOT 0.1 mm!). Always read m AND n!

cards.title: Complete reading & zero-error subtraction protocol
items: 1. Read MSR just LEFT of vernier zero. 2. Multiply coinciding vernier mark k by LC. 3. Algebraically SUBTRACT signed zero reading e0 (E4, P15, P22):
Positive zero error (+e0, vernier 0 right of main 0, mark p coincides): e0 = +p * LC. Negative zero error (-|e0|, vernier 0 left of main 0, mark c coincides in standard n-div scale):

cards.title: Worked readings & negative zero-error verification
items: Exemplar E4: LC = 0.01 cm, zero error e0 = -0.03 cm, MSR = 2.30 cm, 7th vernier mark aligns: x_true = 2.30 + 7(0.01) - (-0.03) = 2.40 cm!
Paper P22: LC = 0.01 cm, e0 = +0.02 cm, MSR = 2.70 cm, 5th mark aligns: x_true = 2.75 - (+0.02) = 2.73 cm.
Physical sanity check: always ask "when jaws touch, did the scale ALREADY read positive (+e0, too high -> subtract) or had not reached zero yet (-|e0|, too low -> add)?"
Notice why negative zero coincidence uses -(n - c) * LC: if vernier 0 shifts left by tiny 0.03 cm, the 7th mark (10 - 3 = 7) lines up, NOT the 3rd mark!

cards.title: Extended / retro-vernier: when 1 VSD > 1 MSD!
items: In some precision callipers (JEE Advanced 2016/2021 style), n vernier divisions span (n + 1) or (2n - 1) main-scale divisions so 1 VSD EXCEEDS 1 MSD!
Because 1 VSD > 1 MSD, vernier gaps WIDEN to the right so coincidence steps backward (retrograde vernier has LC = 1 VSD - 1 MSD = MSD / n)!
Golden habit: writing x = M_coinc * MSD - k * VSD directly from geometry works on EVERY strange custom scale even if numbers look unfamiliar!

title: Screw gauge, spherometer & Young modulus apparatus
subtitle: Pitch and circular scale resolution, zero-offset rules, E10 source audit fix, and classic JEE practical error budgets.
takeaway: LC = Pitch / N_circ; in wire/capillary formulas where diameter d enters to high powers (d^2 or d^4), measuring d with a screw gauge controls total error!
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md sec. 3.11, E10 (fixed!), Q7, P11 + JEE lab apparatus

cards.title: Pitch, circular divisions & screw-gauge reading
items: If advancing the thimble through R full rotations moves the spindle linearly by D along the sleeve scale, pitch P = D / R and least count LC is:
Source E10 audit fix: pitch 0.5 mm, N = 50 -> LC = 0.01 mm. Sleeve shows 3.00 mm, circular = 22, zero error e0 = +0.04 mm -> x_true = 3.00 + 0.22 - 0.04 = 3.18 mm (NOT 3.40 mm in E10 check box!).
Watch half-millimetre sleeve marks! With pitch = 0.5 mm, sleeve ticks show BOTH whole mm and 0.5 mm (e.g. 3.5 mm visible + 22(0.01) = 3.72 mm)!

cards.title: Screw-gauge zero offset & backlash prevention
items: Close anvil & spindle gently using ONLY the ratchet stop: look at circular mark c on reference line with N total circular divisions:
Example: 100-div gauge closed reads mark 97 on reference line (zero has not arrived by 3 div!) -> e0 = -(100 - 97) * 0.01 = -0.03 mm (Q7: 5.38 - (-0.03) = 5.41 mm).
Backlash error arises from play between worn screw threads when reversing rotation direction: ALWAYS approach final reading rotating in ONE direction!

cards.title: Spherometer radius of curvature formula
items: A three-legged spherometer (equilateral leg spacing l, screw pitch P, circular divisions N -> LC = P/N) measures sagitta height h of a spherical cap:
Geometry proof: leg circumradius is r_c = l / sqrt(3), and chord property r_c^2 = h (2 R - h) gives R = l^2/(6 h) + h/2 immediately!
Always take ZERO reading on an optically flat glass plate first, then on the curved mirror/lens surface: h = |h_curved - h_plane|!

cards.title: Searle wire, Poiseuille tube & optical bench budgets
items: Spot which variable carries the largest exponent in JEE lab experiments to know which instrument demands highest precision:
Y = \frac{4 M g L}{\pi d^2 \Delta L} \Rightarrow \frac{\Delta Y}{Y} = \frac{\Delta M}{M} + \frac{\Delta L}{L} + \frac{2\Delta d}{d} + \frac{\Delta(\Delta L)}{\Delta L}
\eta = \frac{\pi \Delta P r^4}{8 Q L} \Rightarrow \frac{\Delta\eta}{\eta}\ \text{carries}\ \mathbf{4}\frac{\Delta r}{r}\ \text{(1\% error in } r \to 4\%\text{ in }\eta\text{!)}
Watch factor 2 mistake on wire diameter vs radius: d = 2 r -> dd/d = dr/r (identical percentage error — NEVER multiply dd/d by another extra 2)!

title: Graph linearisation, slope bounds & Fermi estimation
subtitle: Straightening curved physical laws on log-log, semi-log & reciprocal axes, bounding slopes, and order-of-magnitude modelling.
takeaway: Linearise non-linear laws BEFORE reading constants from data; in Fermi estimates, break unknown scale into 3-4 familiar factors whose logs cancel!
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md sec. 3.12, 7.4, E9, OL7, Q9, Q10, Q24, P12, P19, P25, P26

cards.title: Four standard linearisations every candidate must own
items: Choose plot axes X and Y so your physical model becomes a straight line Y = m X + c whose slope m and intercept c isolate unknown parameters cleanly:
y=a x^n \implies \ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\ (\mathrm{slope}\ n,\ \mathrm{int}\ \ln a)
Multi-correct trap (P19): on a log-log plot of y = a x^n, y-axis intercept at ln x = 0 is ln(a) (or log10 a), NEVER raw constant a itself!

cards.title: Graphical slope & worst-case bounding lines
items: When estimating slope quickly by hand on graph paper: (1) pick two distant points ON THE BEST-FIT LINE (NOT raw data points!); (2) draw steepest m_max and shallowest m_min lines spanning the error bars:
Non-zero y-intercept on T^2 vs L reveals systematic length offset L_eff = L_measured + r_bob: the SLOPE 4 pi^2 / g STILL gives unbiased g unaffected by constant offset r_bob!
Taking ln(y) changes error bar height from dy to dy / y: tiny y points acquire huge log error bars and must NOT outweigh large-y points!

cards.title: Fermi order-of-magnitude estimation protocol
items: Decompose any unfamiliar quantity into a product of 3-5 human-scale factors (random over/underestimates partially cancel in multiplication!):
\mathrm{Geometric\ midpoint\ between\ } a\ \mathrm{and}\ b:\ \ x_{\mathrm{est}} = \sqrt{a b}
Classic atmospheric mass (P25): M_atm = P0 * (4 pi R_E^2) / g = 1e5 * 4 pi (6.4e6)^2 / 9.8 = 5.3e18 kg! Lifetime breaths (E9): 12/min * 5.26e5 min/yr * 70 yr ~ 4.4e8!
Between bounds 10^2 and 10^4, arithmetic average is 5050 (wrong scale!) whereas geometric midpoint sqrt(10^2 * 10^4) = 10^3 hits dead center on log scale!

cards.title: Oleic-acid monolayer thickness & Avogadro check (OL7, P33)
items: Dilute 1 cm^3 oleic acid into alcohol (say 1 : 400 concentration), drop volume V_oil onto water dusted with lycopodium powder to form circular film radius R:
Gives direct tabletop proof that organic molecules have ~1 nm length! Warning (P33): estimating N_A = (M/rho)/(d * sigma) additionally assumes molecular cross-section sigma!

title: Master triage, multi-swing timing & top traps
subtitle: Single-page exam playbook, why timing N swings beats averaging N single swings, and the ten deadliest JEE error traps.
takeaway: Timing N consecutive swings cuts stopwatch reaction error as 1/N (NOT 1/sqrt(N))! Always simplify algebraic duplicates BEFORE differentiating!

cards.title: CRITICAL LAB INSIGHT: 1/N vs 1/sqrt(N) timing law!
items: Suppose human start/stop reaction error on a stopwatch is dt_sw = 0.20 s and pendulum period is T = 2.00 s:
N\ \mathrm{continuous\ swings:}\ t=N T \implies \Delta T = \frac{\Delta t_{\mathrm{sw}}}{N} \propto \frac{1}{N}
At N = 25 swings, continuous timing gives dT = 0.20/25 = 0.008 s (5x BETTER than 25 separate 1-swing runs giving 0.20/5 = 0.040 s in the exact same time)!

cards.title: Top dimensional & sig-fig exam traps
items: Angle trap: rad and sr HAVE units yet NO dimensions [M^0 L^0 T^0]; never say "unitless <=> dimensionless" works both ways!
Hidden constants: s_n = u + (a/2)(2n - 1) IS dimensionally valid because hidden factor (1 s) sits inside every term!
Linear dependency: before rewriting Y in custom bases {X1, X2, X3}, verify det != 0 (e.g. {Energy, Work, Time} or {F, m, a} is INVALID)!
Decimal vs total digits: 15.4 + 0.082 = 15.5 (1 decimal place, 3 sf), whereas 15.4 * 0.082 = 1.3 (2 total sig figs from 0.082)!

cards.title: Top error-propagation & instrument traps
items: Sum percent trap: NEVER add percentage errors on A + B or A - B! Compute dA + dB FIRST, then divide by |A +- B|!
Repeated variable trap: NEVER expand d(R1 R2 / (R1 + R2)) as dR1/R1 + dR2/R2 + (dR1+dR2)/(R1+R2)! Always write 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2 -> dR/R^2 = dR1/R1^2 + dR2/R2^2!
Radian rule: in y = sin(theta), dy = |cos(theta)| d(theta) REQUIRES d(theta) in RADIANS (1 deg = pi/180 rad = 0.01745 rad, NEVER plug "1"!)!
Vernier reading trap: check 1 MSD AND how many MSD equal n VSD before touching LC — custom scales like 10 VSD = 8 mm appear constantly in JEE Advanced!

cards.title: Pre-submission 5-check scorecard
items: 1. Did every exponent come with |p_i| PLUS signs in worst-case propagation (even for denominators C^-r)?
2. Did you check wire DIAMETER vs RADIUS (dd/d == dr/r, so d^2 contributes 2 dd/d, NOT 4)?
3. Did you subtract zero error WITH ITS SIGN: True = Raw - (+e0) and True = Raw - (-|e0|)?
4. Did you distinguish single-trial scatter sigma from standard error of the mean sigma / sqrt(n), and round uncertainty to 1 sig fig?

title: Buckingham Pi theorem & dimensional matrix rank
subtitle: Rigorous linear-algebra proof via nullspace rank, capillary-gravity two-group dispersion, and atomic Bohr scales.
takeaway: Number of independent dimensionless groups is ALWAYS p = n - rank(D), NEVER blind n - k when two base dimensions only enter locked together!
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md OL4, OL8, P28, P31, P34

cards.title: Exact statement via rank of dimensional matrix D
items: List all n physical quantities Q_1, ..., Q_n entering a law f(Q_1, ..., Q_n) = 0, and form the k x n exponent matrix D_ij across k base dimensions:

Rank trap proof: in static Hookean springs {F, k_spr, x}, symbols M, L, T appear (k = 3!), YET D columns are [1,1,-2], [1,0,-2], [0,1,0] with rank r = 2 -> p = 3 - 2 = 1 group Pi = F / (k_spr x)! Blind n - k = 0 would FAIL!

cards.title: Two-Pi masterclass: capillary-gravity water waves
items: Phase speed v on deep water depends on wavenumber k, gravity g, density rho, and surface tension gamma: n = 5 variables across rank r = 3 [M, L, T] -> p = 2 groups!
\Pi_1 = \frac{v}{\sqrt{g / k}}, \qquad \Pi_2 = \frac{\gamma k^2}{\rho g}\ (\text{Bond}^{-1}) \implies v = \sqrt{\frac{g}{k}}\,\Phi\!\left(\frac{\gamma k^2}{\rho g}\right)
Exact hydrodynamics supplies Phi(u) = sqrt(1 + u), giving v = sqrt(g/k + gamma k / rho) with minimum speed v_min = (4 g gamma / rho)^(1/4) = 23.1 cm/s on water!
Without fluid PDEs, Pi theorem ALONE proves minimum speed scales as (g gamma / rho)^(1/4) at wavelength ~ sqrt(gamma / rho g)!

cards.title: Hydrogen Bohr radius & Rydberg energy (OL8, P34)
items: Non-relativistic quantum electrostatics has 4 independent parameters {m_e, e, eps0, hbar} spanning all 4 dimensions [M, L, T, A] (rank r = 4):
Notice: adding speed of light c introduces n = 5th variable at rank 4 -> p = 1 dimensionless group alpha = e^2/(4 pi eps0 hbar c) ~ 1/137 (fine-structure splitting ~ alpha^2 |E_1|)!

cards.title: Trinity nuclear test & prefactor caution (OL9, P28)
items: For Trinity 1945 (E = 84 TJ, t = 0.025 s, R = 100 m), naive inversion rho ~ E t^2 / R^5 (setting k = 1 in R = k (E t^2 / rho)^(1/5)) gives:

Why off by 4.2x? Because k enters raised to the FIFTH POWER: G. I. Taylor solved the adiabatic shock ODE for air (gamma = 1.4) to get k = 1.033 (1.033^5 = 1.18; remaining factor is yield calibration)!
Whenever solving backwards for a quantity inside a 1/5 power, a tiny 20% uncertainty in k or R explodes by factor (1.2)^5 = 2.5x!

title: Dynamical similarity, scale models & allometry
subtitle: Matching dimensionless groups in wind tunnels & towing tanks, conflict of simultaneous Re + Fr matching, and Galileo scaling.
takeaway: A scale model reproduces full non-linear physics faithfully IF AND ONLY IF every relevant dimensionless Pi group has the exact same numerical value!
source: Source: Olympiad physical similarity & scaling toolkit (INPhO / IPhO standard)

cards.title: Four master dimensionless numbers of continuum physics
items: Divide competing force terms in Navier-Stokes / elasticity to extract universal regime numbers without solving the PDE:
Sphere drag F = (1/2) C_D(Re) rho pi r^2 v^2 unifies BOTH regimes: for Re << 1, C_D = 24/Re recovers linear Stokes drag 6 pi eta r v; for Re ~ 10^4, C_D ~ 0.47 gives quadratic drag!

cards.title: Wind-tunnel & ship-hull model scaling dilemma
items: Test a 1:25 scale aircraft wing (L_m / L_p = 1/25) or ship hull in the laboratory by keeping Pi_model = Pi_prototype:
Classic IPhO trap: in the SAME fluid at fixed g, Re requires v_m ~ L^-1 while Fr requires v_m ~ L^+1/2 -> BOTH can match ONLY in a fluid of kinematic viscosity nu_m = nu_p (L_m/L_p)^(3/2)!

cards.title: Mechanical & gravitational self-similarity
items: Scale every linear dimension of a structure or planet uniformly by factor lambda (L -> lambda L) at fixed material density rho and strength sigma_max:
Galileo square-cube law: doubling an animal height without thickening proportions doubles bone stress! Constant safety factor requires bone diameter d ~ L^(3/2)!
Self-gravitating homogeneous sphere: surface g = (4/3) pi G rho R ~ R^1, free-fall / orbital period T_orb = sqrt(3 pi / G rho) ~ R^0 (INDEPENDENT of planet size R)!

cards.title: Jumping animals, cooling rates & heat loss scaling
items: Compare maximal vertical jump height h of geometrically similar animals (muscle work W_muscle = sigma_muscle * A_muscle * s_stroke ~ L^2 * L = L^3!):
m g h \sim W_{\mathrm{muscle}} \implies (\lambda^3) g h \sim \lambda^3 \implies h \propto \lambda^0
Heat-loss timescale of a warm body of heat capacity M c ~ L^3 losing heat across skin area A ~ L^2 scales as tau_cool ~ L^1: small shrews must eat continuously!
Always state which material parameters stay constant during scaling (e.g. constant density rho vs constant total mass M changes every exponent)!

title: Least-squares regression, normal equations & errors
subtitle: Exact derivation of OLS slope/intercept, standard errors sigma_b and sigma_a, x-vs-y asymmetry, and weighted fits.
takeaway: OLS line ALWAYS passes through centroid (x_bar, y_bar) with b = S_xy / S_xx and sigma_b = sigma_y / sqrt(S_xx) — spread x_i wide!
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md OL1, OL2, P18, P30

cards.title: Normal equations & centroid theorem (OL1, P18)
items: For n pairs (x_i, y_i) with exact x_i and independent equal-variance vertical errors sigma_y, minimise S(a, b) = sum_i (y_i - a - b x_i)^2:
Setting dS/da = 0 immediately forces y_bar = a + b x_bar: EVERY unconstrained best-fit line passes strictly through centroid (x_bar, y_bar), NOT (0, 0)!
Regressing x on y gives slope b_xy = S_xy / S_yy != 1 / b_yx: their product b_yx * b_xy = r^2 <= 1 equals squared Pearson correlation!

cards.title: Standard errors of slope sigma_b & intercept sigma_a (OL2)
items: Notice b = sum_i c_i y_i is linear in y_i with weights c_i = (x_i - x_bar)/S_xx satisfying sum c_i^2 = 1/S_xx. Propagating variance gives:
Look at n - 2 in residual scatter sigma_y: fitting TWO parameters (a, b) consumes 2 degrees of freedom (with just n = 2 points, line hits both exactly so residuals = 0)!

cards.title: Worked full Olympiad exam drill (Paper P30)
items: Design rule: placing half your trials near x_min and half near x_max maximizes S_xx (after verifying linearity with interior points)!

cards.title: Through-origin slope & unequal error bars (WLS)
items: 1. If physics GUARANTEES zero intercept (y = b x with zero offset verified), minimising sum (y_i - b x_i)^2 gives:
2. When error bars sigma_i vary from point to point (e.g. after taking ln y!), weight every point by inverse variance w_i = 1 / sigma_i^2:

title: Chi-square goodness of fit, weighted mean & covariance
subtitle: Testing models quantitatively with chi^2/(n - p), optimal inverse-variance data fusion, and full correlated error propagation.
takeaway: A trustworthy fit of p parameters to n data points satisfies chi^2 ~ (n - p) +- sqrt(2(n - p)); combining measurements weights strictly by 1/sigma_i^2!
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md OL3, P30(c) + Olympiad statistical analysis

cards.title: Chi-square test statistic & degrees of freedom (OL3)
items: For n independent Gaussian measurements y_i +- sigma_i fitted by a theoretical curve f(x_i; theta_1, ..., theta_p) having p adjustable parameters:
Each standardised residual z_i = r_i / sigma_i ~ N(0, 1) contributes E[z_i^2] = 1, minus p fitted constraints: E[chi^2] = nu and SD(chi^2) = sqrt(2 nu)!
Check P30(c): residuals {+0.01, -0.13, +0.23, -0.11} with sigma = 0.2 give chi^2 = 2.05 for nu = 4 - 2 = 2 (chi^2_nu = 1.03 ~ 1 -> textbook fit!).

cards.title: Three diagnostic outcomes of reduced chi^2_nu
items: 1. chi^2_nu ~ 1 (within 1 +- sqrt(2/nu)): model AND stated uncertainties sigma_i are mutually consistent.
2. chi^2_nu >> 1 (e.g. chi^2 = 45 for nu = 8): EITHER model is missing real physics (curvature / systematic drift) OR error bars sigma_i were underestimated!
3. chi^2_nu << 1 (e.g. chi^2 = 0.4 for nu = 10): NOT "miraculously accurate data" — your error bars sigma_i are way too conservative (or data was overfitted/fudged)!

cards.title: Optimal combination of independent labs (weighted mean)
items: Two or more independent experiments measure the SAME physical constant with different precisions x_1 +- sigma_1, ..., x_k +- sigma_k. Minimising chi^2(mu) = sum (x_i - mu)^2 / sigma_i^2 gives:
Combined precision ALWAYS beats every individual experiment! If sigma_1 = 0.01 and sigma_2 = 0.10, Run 1 carries weight 100x larger than Run 2 — NEVER take unweighted mean (x1+x2)/2!

cards.title: Correlated errors & covariance matrix formula
items: Whenever two fitted quantities (such as OLS intercept a and slope b, with Cov(a, b) = -x_bar sigma_y^2 / S_xx < 0!) derive from the SAME dataset, use covariance C_xy = <dx dy>:

\sigma_f^2 = \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\right)^2\sigma_x^2 + \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}\right)^2\sigma_y^2 + 2\left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\right)\left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}\right)\mathrm{Cov}(x, y)
Look how nicely this explains extrapolating y_hat(x) = a + b x: plug Cov(a, b) in and cross-term cancels x_bar to give exact confidence fan:

title: Poisson counting statistics, background & dead time
subtitle: Exact sqrt(N) shot noise, rigorous background-subtraction formula (fixing P35c), optimal time splitting, and Geiger dead time.
takeaway: Subtracting background REQUIRES ADDING variances: sigma(R_net) = sqrt(R_tot / t_on + R_b / t_off); NEVER substitute R_net inside the square root!
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md sec. 7.3, OL6, P16, P35 (audited & extended)

cards.title: Poisson event counts & the universal sqrt(N) law (OL6)
items: Independent random point events at mean rate R over time t follow Poisson law P(k) = mu^k exp(-mu) / k! with mean mu = R t and exact standard deviation:
Worked OL6: N = 10,000 counts in 600 s gives 1% precision (16.67 +- 0.17 s^-1). Reaching 0.1% demands N = 10^6 counts -> 100x longer run (16.7 hours)!
CRITICAL TRAP: apply sqrt(.) ONLY to raw integer COUNTS N, NEVER to rate R! If 100 counts arrive in 10 s, R = 10 +- 1 s^-1 (NOT 10 +- sqrt(10) = 10 +- 3.16)!

cards.title: Exact background subtraction (audit of Paper P35c!)
items: Count source+background for t_on (observing N_tot = R_tot t_on) and pure background separately for t_off (observing N_b = R_b t_off):

Audit note on P35(c): with R_tot = 250/s (R_s = 200/s) and R_b = 50/s, if R_b is known with zero error then sigma(R_net) = sqrt(2500)/10 = 5.0/s; ONLY when R_b is ALSO measured for 10 s (N_b = 500) does variance become (2500 + 500)/10^2 -> 5.48/s!

cards.title: Optimal beam-time split for fixed total lab time T
items: Given fixed total detector time T = t_on + t_off, minimise variance V = R_tot / t_on + R_b / (T - t_on) with respect to t_on:
Clean physical limits: if signal >> background (R_tot >> R_b), spend almost all time on source; if weak signal sits atop huge background (R_tot ~ R_b), split 50% / 50%!

cards.title: Detector dead time tau (non-paralysable model)
items: After each registered click, a Geiger/scintillation counter stays blind for dead time tau. In 1 second it registers m clicks and is dead for total fraction m * tau:
m = R_{\mathrm{true}}(1 - m\tau) \implies R_{\mathrm{true}} = \frac{m}{1 - m\tau}, \qquad m = \frac{R_{\mathrm{true}}}{1 + R_{\mathrm{true}}\tau}
At intense rates R_true >> 1/tau, observed count rate saturates at ceiling 1/tau AND sub-Poisson anti-bunching breaks naive sqrt(N) statistics!
Two-source lab calibration: measure m1, m2 separately and m12 together -> m1 + m2 > m12 reveals dead time tau directly without knowing R_true!

title: Olympiad experiment design: 0.1% g-budget & natural units
subtitle: End-to-end error budget engineering (OL5 / P32), systematic corrections on real pendulums, and symmetry scaling laws.
takeaway: In experiment design, list EVERY random AND systematic term in dg/g BEFORE touching equipment, and engineer every term well below ceiling!
source: Source: units-measurements/Units-measurements.md OL5, OL10, P27, P32, P36

cards.title: Engineering a 0.10% measurement of g (OL5, P32)
items: Available gear: ruler (dL = 1 mm), stopwatch (dt = 0.01 s), string up to 2 m, steel bob. Target: dg / g < 0.10% from g = 4 pi^2 L / T^2:
Design choices: 1. Max out length L = 2.000 m so dL/L = 1/2000 = 0.050%. 2. Now T = 2.84 s; time N = 50 continuous swings (142 s) so 2 dt/(N T) = 0.014%!
3. Restrict launch angle to theta_0 = 2 deg = 0.0349 rad so 2(theta_0^2/16) = 0.015%! Total budget = 0.050 + 0.014 + 0.015 = 0.079% < 0.10%!

cards.title: Three hidden physical systematics in real pendulums
items: To trust 0.1% accuracy (not merely precision!), account for three real-world physics corrections beyond point-mass vacuum theory:
I_{\mathrm{pivot}} = m L^2 + \frac{2}{5} m r_{\mathrm{bob}}^2 \implies L_{\mathrm{eff}} = L_{\mathrm{cm}}\!\left(1 + \frac{2 r_{\mathrm{bob}}^2}{5 L_{\mathrm{cm}}^2}\right)
Plus time zero-crossings AT EQUILIBRIUM (fastest bob speed -> sharpest visual trigger!), NEVER at extreme turning points where v = 0!

cards.title: Relativistic corrections via symmetry + dimensions (OL10, P36)
items: How must momentum p = m v f(v/c) or rod length L = L0 g(v/c) behave at small speeds beta = v/c BEFORE invoking full Lorentz algebra?

Spatial isotropy + smoothness at v = 0 forbids odd linear terms +-v/c in scalar factor f! Special relativity fixes alpha_1 = +1/2 for momentum (1% shift at v = 0.141 c, P36) and -1/2 for Lorentz contraction!

cards.title: Natural units c = hbar = k_B = 1 (theoretical Olympiad tool)
items: In particle/astrophysics Olympiad problems using natural units (hbar = c = k_B = 1), EVERY mechanical/thermal quantity collapses onto powers of ENERGY [E]:
To restore hbar and c at the end of any derivation, uniquely match [M, L, T]: e.g. energy density [u] = [E^4] restores to u ~ (k_B T)^4 / (hbar c)^3 (Stefan-Boltzmann T^4 scaling in ONE second)!
Handy anchor: hbar c = 197.3 MeV fm = 197.3 eV nm!
